academicReview.strongestChallenge: Coherence and a limitation note alone are insufficient. The target defines an empirical social-scientific and legal study of crime and societal responses. UCR directly teaches criminal responsibility, punishment, case reasoning and organised-crime inquiry in Criminal Law & Criminal Justice; Law, Society & Justice examines socio-legal relationships. Substantial sociology/psychology, qualitative/quantitative methods, rights and public-institution study provide an academically related response, with an actual youth-prevention application in the closest option. These are bounded taught contributions, not assumed crime topics in arbitrary projects.

programmes.concept: Criminal responsibility and justice connect with sociology, social psychology and empirical research. Legal study, rights and social theory provide perspectives on crime and social responses, while developmental psychology and youth resilience offer specific behavioural and prevention-related contributions.
programmes.judgment: Preserve the broad socio-legal/behavioural response. Developmental and abnormal psychology are complementary background, not taught criminal-career or forensic-psychology equivalents. Victimology remains a disclosed gap.

programmes.concept: Criminal law, rights and constitutional study connect with political authority, ethics and European institutions. Sociology and empirical methods support the study of law and society, while public economics adds a general framework for assessing public intervention.
programmes.judgment: Preserve the distinct institutional/normative response. Its additional political philosophy, EU politics, ethics and public economics implement public-authority inquiry; no dedicated crime-policy evaluation or safety-planning sequence is asserted.

stopping.assessment: One additional evidenced institutional/legal direction is feasible and differs by four courses/30 EC. A separate victimisation/support direction was considered: human rights, social psychology and media/race supply particular perspectives but do not establish a materially distinct, sustained 24-course victimology/support programme from the current catalogue. No third option is manufactured. Crime-prevention interest 18 is assigned to the closest option, which actually includes the youth-resilience application; specialist crime-prevention and victimology limits remain explicit.
